verdicts.reason: Photo shows a blurred mother holding a newborn baby with a nursery mobile in the foreground — an evocative new-mother scene that is adjacent to matrescence but does not name or represent the psychological transformation itself.

Photo shows a woman dressed as a judge with a grey wig and scales of justice behind her, representing judgment/being judged — thematically adjacent to the affirmation's subject of having one's spiritual practice judged, but it depicts legal judgment not spiritual judgment.

Photo shows a neon sign reading 'TIME IS PRECIOUS' on a building exterior — picks up the time theme of the affirmation but is a decorative sign, not a visual representation of time being 'enough' or the affirmation practice itself.
Photo shows a pile of brown and orange needle-felted wool balls, not a needle-felted bee — completely different felted subject with no bee visible.

Photo shows a needle-felted white figure hanging as a Christmas tree ornament — it is a needle-felted hanging ornament, the right class, but the figure appears to be a snowman or elf rather than a robin-coloured bird.
Photo shows a pile of brown and orange needle-felted wool balls, not a needle-felted hedgehog — completely different felted subject with no hedgehog visible.
Photo shows a needle-felted grey rabbit with upright ears surrounded by colourful pom-poms, directly matching the tutorial's subject of a needle-felted sitting rabbit in grey merino.
Photo shows real live sheep and lambs grazing in a field, not the needle-felted miniature sheep flock that is the tutorial's subject.

Photo shows needle-felted wool spheres, which are simple 3D felted forms related to the armature-free sculpture technique, but they are basic balls rather than the finished animal or abstract sculptural forms the tutorial covers.

Photo shows a person's arm draped in flowing sheer white organza fabric — shows the organza material used in nuno felting but not the felting process or the characteristic textured, pleated nuno-felted cloth.

Photo shows candles sitting on small wooden dishes on a table — shows candles on a tray-like surface which is the use case for an oak candle tray, but the wooden tray itself is not an identifiable oak piece with chamfered edges.
Photo shows One Piece manga volumes (vol. 31) — books, not clothing or the act of wearing a fashion piece someone has deemed too young.

Photo shows a lit candle, dried herbs, and a piece of paper with text on a wooden bedside surface — a contemplative prayer/ritual still life that evokes the ritual setting, but no person is shown speaking a sentence of prayer.
Photo shows the word 'ONE' painted in large white letters on a blue brick wall — textually connects to 'one small thing' but is street art typography, not an image of doing a small manageable task.

Photo shows vibrantly dyed tie-dye fabric in rainbow colours — shows dyed textile which is the right class of output, but tie-dye is a resist-dyeing technique distinct from overdyeing, and no dye bath or fibre/yarn is visible.
Photo shows a pile of white wheat flour with a wheat stalk and a wooden spoon — a key ingredient, not the finished Pain rustique loaf.

Photo shows a sliced rustic white Italian-style loaf with thick crust, which is the right class of bread for pane pugliese, but the crumb appears tighter and more even than the open, moist crumb characteristic of this Apulian loaf.
Photo shows chocolate bars or bark coated with chopped pistachios and walnuts on a plate — chocolate nut confectionery, not peanut butter brownies with a peanut butter swirl.
Photo shows flour pouring from an overturned glass jar onto a wooden surface — an ingredient shot of flour, not the finished Yorkshire pikelets.

Photo shows multiple spice jars with metal lids arranged on rustic wooden shelving — shows the use case of a spice rack holding jars, but the rack is not identifiably pine wood and no construction detail is visible.
Photo shows three brown eggs on a floured surface — eggs are a key ingredient for pizzelle but this is an ingredient shot, not the finished thin crisp Italian waffle biscuits.
Photo shows a pan-fried pork chop topped with diced caramelised apple and onion with broccolini on a white plate — unambiguously matches the tutorial's pork chops with cider and apples dish.

Photo shows a plate with what appears to be a ground-meat patty or meatball-type item, sweet potato mash, and green beans — a different dish entirely, with no pork chop or mustard cream sauce visible.
Photo shows raw pork shoulder and belly cuts laid out on a wooden board — uncooked raw meat, not the finished hot-water-crust pork pie.

Photo shows cooked shrimp/prawns being drained from a pot into a colander — shows the key ingredient being cooked and handled, but not the finished potted shrimp packed into ramekins and sealed with spiced clarified butter.
Photo shows a tray of whole cooked prawns with heads on — shows the key ingredient (cooked prawns) but not the finished prawn cocktail presentation with Marie Rose sauce, shredded lettuce, and lemon.
Photo shows a decorative ceramic tea cup placed on a plain wooden disc — a tea cup on an undecorated wooden surface, with no pyrography burn marks, leaf design, or fire-work visible.
Photo shows a person studying financial or stock-market line charts on paper — a completely different type of chart from a weaving sett chart, different domain entirely.

Photo shows a neat white floating shelf with books, small potted plants, and a figurine arranged on it — directly and unambiguously depicts a styled shelf, which is the subject of the rearrange-one-shelf activity.
Photo shows colourful needle-felted wool balls — dryer balls or decorative felted spheres, not a resist-felted bowl shape.

Photo shows a floor loom (shaft loom) with white warp threads and heddles — weaving equipment in the right domain, but this is a multi-shaft floor loom, not the rigid heddle loom used in the tutorial.

Photo shows a person hammering a modern plastic/metal tent peg into the ground with a rubber mallet — shows the use case of tent pegs being driven in, but the peg is a manufactured metal one, not a hand-riven oak wooden peg.

Photo shows a sliced dense dark rye loaf with close-grained crumb on a wooden board — the characteristic appearance of Roggenbrot, matching the tutorial's description of a dense, close-crumbed German rye bread.
Photo shows devilled eggs on a tray — a completely different food item from Scandinavian rosettes, which are thin crisp fried batter cookies.

Photo shows a generous slice of a pastry-lidded pie with chunky filling on a plate with chips and greens — right class of dish (meat pie with pastry crust), but the filling looks like chicken or pork rather than salmon, and no dill is evident.
Photo shows meatballs in an orange sauce with polenta or mashed potato — a different dish entirely from sausage and mash with caramelised onions.
Photo shows two grilled bratwurst-style sausages on a plate with mustard — plain grilled sausages, not a sausage roll (no puff pastry encasing the sausagemeat).
Photo shows a pile of whole raw langoustines (Norway lobsters) at a market — the correct shellfish ingredient for scampi, but not the finished breaded and deep-fried dish.

Photo shows hands pressing and stretching flat bread dough on a floured surface — shows the technique stage of forming a flatbread, which is adjacent to schiacciata, but no grapes are pressed into it and the characteristic topping is absent.

Photo shows a bowl of clear broth soup with chunks of meat and root vegetables — shows the right class of dish (lamb and vegetable broth), but courgette and black beans are present instead of the pearl barley, swede, and leek of Scotch broth.
Photo shows raw red mince meat in a glass bowl — an uncooked ingredient, not the finished Shepherd's Pie with lamb filling under a mashed-potato crust.
Photo shows sliced leeks on a wooden cutting board with a knife — an ingredient being prepped, not the finished smoked haddock and leek pie.
Photo shows mixing bowls with dry baking ingredients and measuring cups of liquid — a baking ingredient prep shot, not the finished griddle-cooked soda farls.
Photo shows a sliced banana loaf on a board alongside whole and sliced bananas — directly and unambiguously shows banana bread, which is the tutorial subject.

Photo shows a bowl of waffle batter in the foreground with waffles and blueberries visible in the background — waffles are present and identifiable but the batter bowl dominates rather than the finished waffles; the specific sourdough character cannot be seen.
Photo shows a close-up portrait of a grey-blue faced sheep (which may be a BFL breed) — shows the animal that provides the fleece, but not the spinning process, drafting, or finished BFL yarn.

Photo shows hands drafting white wool fibre into a thin singles thread at a spinning wheel — clearly shows the spinning technique and wool fibre being worked, directly matching the tutorial's subject.

Photo shows an industrial silk-processing facility with large hanks of yellow/gold silk fibre hanging to dry and reeling equipment — shows silk fibre at scale, the right material class, but not the specific Mawata silk hankie product or the act of drafting from a hankie on a spindle.

Photo shows a restaurant-plated dish with a golden polenta/cornmeal round topped with mushroom, tomatoes, and kale — a polenta-based dish in the right class, but plated as a formal restaurant dish rather than the soft spoonable baked cornmeal pudding that is spoonbread.
Photo shows raw beef fillet steaks on a board next to a dish of sliced raw potatoes — raw meat and potato ingredients, not the finished steak and ale pie with braised chuck under a pastry lid.
